angle: The financial cost of under-leveraging high income in property investment, positioning strategic upgrading as a wealth-building imperative.
body_text:
If your household income is $20K/month… but your property is under $3M… you might be quietly losing $40K–$50K a year.

Let me explain why

Hey, it’s Chris here.

Let me share a quick story about David and Sarah.

Good income, stable careers, living in a comfortable condo, everything looked perfectly fine.

But when we reviewed their numbers… they realised they were making the #1 mistake high earners make:

Holding an asset that was too small for their income capacity.

Not small in space.

Small in asset size.

Most people fear upgrading because of “bigger payments”.

But here’s what they don’t see: when your income grows but your asset doesn’t

You’re wasting your peak leverage window

The period where banks lend more, tenure is long, and compounding works hardest.

Once David and Sarah understood this, the decision became clear.

They didn’t upgrade for lifestyle.

They upgraded for growth.

And now their assets work significantly harder — without taking reckless risks.

Here are 3 insights most high earners overlook:

INSIGHT #1 — Your 30s–40s are your leverage peak.
Miss it, and you can’t get it back.

INSIGHT #2 — “Comfortable” can be costly.

Staying put often means your wealth stays put too.

INSIGHT #3 — The right loan structure reduces risk, not increases it.

Financing optimisation is the real unlock.

That’s why I created a full breakdown for families earning $20k/month or more.

Inside, you’ll discover:

 ✅ Why most high earners under-leverage

 ✅ How to upgrade safely without stretching

 ✅ The 3 projects showing strong potential this year

Click Learn More and I’ll send it over

No pressure, no hard sell.

transcript_text: If your household income is $20K a month and your property is worth less than $3 million, you're effectively losing $45,000 a year. Let me explain to you why. Hey, it's Chris here. Let me tell you a story about David and Sarah. Their combined income is about $22,000 a month. They live in a $2 million condo in District 16. Everything is good, comfortable and safe. But when I showed them the math, they realized that they were making the most expensive mistake that high earners make. Let me explain. At their 22k household income, their TDSR loan was actually 2.3 to 2.4M, which means they could be holding a 3 to 3.5 million property instead. But Sarah asked me, won't the monthly payment kill us? Here's the thing that most people don't understand. The loan size might be bigger, but the equity that you're holding is massively bigger. Here's the opportunity cost. A 2M property appreciating at 3% per year is $60,000 a year. A 3.5 million property appreciating at 3% a year is 105K a year. That's a 45K difference. Just because of the asset size. Over 10 years, the difference won't be just 450,000. With compounding and market cycles it may even be 700K to 1M difference If you between 30 to 45 years old this is your peak leverage window Banks will lend you more and your income supports a bigger quantum And you got 20 to 30 years for compounding to work. But after 45 years old, the loan tenure shrinks, the window closes. Six months after I showed David and Sarah this, they sold their 2M property and bought a 3.5 million property in District 5. Even though their monthly payment increased, it was still manageable at their income level. But their asset is now 80% larger. But over the next 10 years, they are projected to make $600,000 to $900,000 more wealth than if they had state put. Everything I shared is just the foundation. There's one critical insight that makes their upgrade possible. It's about financing optimization. How to structure loans effectively without increasing risk. But this video is already getting too long. If your household income is $20k per month or more and you're sitting on a property less than $3 million, I've put together a PDF for you. You'll discover why most 20k earners are under leveraging, how to upgrade from 2M to 3.5M property without over leveraging, which are the three projects that have strong potential upside this year. Click on learn more and I'll send it over to you. If Singaporeans like David and Sarah can grow their wealth this way, you can too.
